sentences.text: Revenue moved from $41.9 billion in FY2016 to $47.9 billion in FY2025, a 1.5% CAGR [F1][F10][F219].
The path was a step down then a rebuild: revenue fell 13.5% in FY2017 and 5.3% in FY2018, then compounded 3.7% a year from FY2022 to FY2025 [D42][D93][D782].
The FY2017 decline came with refranchising of bottling operations, which cut operating cash flow by 20% that year [P75].
FY2025 was the sharpest inflection, with operating income up 37.7% on lower other operating charges after the prior-year fairlife contingent consideration remeasurement [D450][P12].
In FY2025 concentrate operations contributed 1.6pp of the 1.9% revenue growth and were 59.4% of revenue [D534][D449][D532].
Finished product operations in the US added 1.3pp while non-US finished product operations subtracted 1.0pp [D562][D555].
Worldwide concentrate sales volume grew 1% in FY2025 while unit case volume was even [P16].
Operating costs grew 9.7pp slower than revenue in FY2025, at cost of revenue growth of 0.4% and SG&A down 0.4% [D474][D465][D466].
Diluted EPS grew 23.6% against net income growth of 23.3% as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D453][D451][D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% in FY2025 was above the 26.0% window median and at the window high, versus a 20.7% low in FY2016 [F50][D766][D765][D764].
Gross margin of 61.6% sat above its 60.7% window median and below the 62.1% high [F30][D772][D771].
The 7.5pp operating margin gain in FY2025 came mostly from the 6.2pp other-lines residual, reflecting lower other operating charges after the fairlife remeasurement [D463][D477][P12].
In FY2025 net margin of 27.3% sat 1.4pp below the 28.7% operating margin, with a 17.9% effective tax rate [F70][F50][D810][D435].
Operating cash flow of $7.41 billion was 0.57x net income in FY2025, below the 1.18x window median and the window low [F100][D436][D800][D799].
Free cash flow of $5.30 billion was a 11.0% margin, below the 20.2% window median [F120][D433][D775].
The FY2024 collapse to $6.81 billion operating cash flow was driven primarily by the $6.0 billion IRS Tax Litigation Deposit [F99][P22].
Capex of $2.11 billion was 4.4% of revenue and 2.01x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F110][D432][D438].
Net debt was $32.4 billion in FY2023, net cash of -70.7% of revenue, but total debt is not reported after FY2023 so later net cash is omitted [D341][D342][X194].
The current ratio rose to 1.46x in FY2025, above the 1.13x window median and at the window high [F200][D781][D780].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.53 billion were 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, against 65.4% in FY2021 [D444][D445][D242].
Return on average equity of 46.0% was above the 36.5% staples peer median, at the 67th percentile of six peers [D448][D798][D797].
Revenue for FY2017 and FY2018 in the table is a later recast, $36.2 billion and $34.3 billion versus $35.4 billion and $31.9 billion first reported [F2][X2][F3][X3].
Growth and margins spanning those years mix two presentations, so the FY2017 and FY2018 comparisons are not clean [R1].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, at 105.1%, 214.2% and 179.9% [D344][D395][D445].
Payout above free cash flow for three years leaves little room if conversion stays weak [R2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [D387][D437].
Cash conversion at the window low is the metric that most undercuts the earnings growth story [R3].
Whether operating cash flow to net income recovers above the 1.18x window median from 0.57x in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D436][D800].
Whether operating margin holds above the 26.0% window median from 28.7% in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [F50][D766].
Whether buybacks plus dividends fall below 179.9% of free cash flow in FY2025, in the FY2026 10-K [D445].
